rule: Any action that makes content publicly visible (publish, schedule entry, merge-with-deploy, send-email, make-repo-public) requires explicit founder go-ahead for that specific action, not just a passing quality gate or completed script.
check: PreToolUse/git-hook blocking writes to known publish surfaces (schedule.yaml commits, calls to publish/update-post scripts, `gh repo edit --visibility public`, social-post API calls) unless an explicit per-post approval marker is present
misses: novel or unenumerated publish paths, and tools whose side effects aren't obviously publish-related (e.g. an 'update' script that quietly republishes) — exactly the failure mode the incident described

rule: When the founder asks a question, answer it directly; do not convert it into an operation or re-ask for authority already granted.
Spawn cheap research agents freely at every phase of dispatch-metrics/capability-discovery work to check documented ground truth before interpreting raw measurements.
When a request names a specific real place/person/creature/product/event, research the real referent before generating art or content about it, rather than fabricating details.
Oblivion compute is free to use autonomously; any scorer/judge or generator round on metered subscriptions (codex/gpt-5.4, Claude/Sonnet) requires a founder decision per round, not standing approval.
check: wrapper-script around the judge/scorer dispatch entrypoint (e.g. cli-dispatch) that refuses to target Sonnet/codex backends unless an explicit per-round approval flag/token is supplied
misses: direct API calls or ad-hoc prompts that invoke Sonnet/codex as a judge without going through the flagged dispatch entrypoint

rule: Autonomous deployment (scoped to the fleet-dispatch system) is authorized only when the step is reversible via a concrete, noted undo mechanism; non-reversible steps fall back to founder-gated.
When a safety hook denies an action for reasoning that is factually wrong, retry once with cleaner phrasing/smaller scope, then stop and hand off to the user rather than constructing workarounds.

Mark uncertain claims with their epistemic status (measured/inferred/guess) inline and never state a hypothesis in the same confident register as a verified fact, especially when briefing other agents.

The oblivion DGX Spark can be taken down for experiments without founder authorization, but the reconciler/timer must still be paused first and trap-guaranteed restore used afterward, per the FM checklist.
check: wrapper-script for tearing down the oblivion inference endpoint that mechanically pauses the reconciler timer and registers a trap to restore it on exit
misses: manual kubectl/docker commands run outside the wrapper, and the remaining judgment-based items in the FM runbook checklist that aren't reducible to pause/restore

rule: A self-authored PR may be merged without a per-PR ask once an independent agent has adversarially verified it (ran tests itself, tried to refute) and CI is re-confirmed green at merge time, excluding irreversible/infra-adjacent-repo/branch-protection-override cases.
check: branch protection requiring a distinct 'independently-verified' status check plus all required CI checks green before the merge button is enabled
misses: whether the verification agent actually ran the tests itself and tried to refute rather than rubber-stamping a status post, and whether the PR falls into an excluded irreversible/infra-adjacent category

rule: During any work, watch for genuine Substack article-worthy moments (irony, a system's own success signal being the story) and capture them as a collect-only note with supporting evidence, without drafting the full article.

For irreversible/high-blast-radius requests, surface risk and any newly-discovered conflicting facts via a clarifying question, then respect an explicit informed yes rather than re-litigating a third time on the same information.

Because no human review-hours exist, authority granted once is standing until revoked or facts change, and the fleet should prefer mechanized trust (verdict gates, adversarial panels, deterministic scoring) over asking again.
